what: spec_context_v55.json under bot v57 (2026-10-18). Everything in spec_context.json and spec_context_v55.json holds, except where the rules below say otherwise. The labels of 'orders' are spec_v57.json's (47 intents; SWITCH_WEAPON and RELOAD are new since v55). Written after the owner's play (2026-10-16..18, 689 lines): lines that lean on the order before them were written back as they were. 'Get inside of it.' right after 'Get to the car.' sent the bot indoors; 'Keep moving.', 'Further up.', 'Move out.' (in the car) made it ask 'Say again?'. Earlier lines are up to five, said in the last 30 seconds, oldest first.
rules: 5b. A pronoun that stands for the thing the last order named ('it', 'them', 'that', 'in it', 'inside of it', 'into it', 'through it', 'on it', 'there' meaning that thing) makes the line incomplete, however complete it looks: put the thing in, in the words the earlier line used for it. before: ['get to the car']; line: 'get inside of it' -> 'Get in the car.' (GET_IN). before: ['go to the north door']; line: 'open it' -> 'Open the north door.' (OPEN). before: ['move up to that window']; line: 'now jump through it' -> 'Jump through that window.' (VAULT_WINDOW). before: ['check the basement']; line: 'and clear it' -> 'Clear the basement.' (ENTRY). before: ['go to the red stairs']; line: 'watch them' -> 'Watch the red stairs.' (HOLD_ANGLE). A pronoun with nothing in the talk for it to stand for ('get inside of it' with no earlier line about a thing) stays as it is. 'there', 'here', 'this', 'that' + a noun that point at the world keep pointing (rule 8): 'go there' stays 'go there'.

5c. A vehicle the talk is about: getting in ('get in', 'hop in', 'jump in', 'get inside', 'get into it', 'sit in it', 'take a seat', 'start riding', 'drive it') after an order about a car or a truck is getting into that vehicle: 'Get in the car.' (GET_IN; the bot sits, it does not drive). Getting out ('get out', 'hop out', 'jump out', 'move out', 'out of it', 'leave the car') after the bot got in (the last order was GET_IN, or the bot said 'In the car.', 'I'm in.', 'Getting in.') is 'Get out of the car.' (GET_OUT). With no vehicle in the talk, 'get out' and 'move out' stay as they are.

12. Going on with a movement: a line that only says to go on or further ('keep moving', 'continue moving', 'keep going', 'go on', 'further', 'further up', 'a bit more', 'more up', 'move up more', 'and up', 'closer', 'a little closer') right after an order that moved the bot is that movement again, written with 'further' or 'more' and the earlier order's way or place, NOT with 'keep' or 'continue' (the classifier reads 'keep moving forward' as no order, 'move further forward' as MOVE_TO; checked 2026-10-18): before: ['go up by the stairs']; line: 'further up' -> 'Go further up by the stairs.' (MOVE_TO). before: ['move forward']; line: 'keep moving' -> 'Move further forward.' (MOVE_TO). before: ['move up']; line: 'more up' -> 'Move up more.' (MOVE_TO). before: ['go left']; line: 'keep going' -> 'Move further left.' (MOVE_TO). before: ['come back to me']; line: 'keep coming' -> 'Come back to me.' (COME_BACK). before: ['come closer to me']; line: 'closer' -> 'Come closer to me.' (FOLLOW_ME). After an order that did not move the bot, or with nothing before it, the line stays as it is (and 'keep moving' alone is no order the bot can carry out: NONE).

13. A repeat that names a place or a side ('try again at my pin', 'try again relocating to my pin', 'do it again over there', 'once more on the left', 'do the same here') is written back AS IT IS, like a bare repeat (rule 1b): its order is REPEAT, and the game repeats the last order at that place.

6c. A 'no' followed by an order of its own right after an order (not only after the bot's question) is that order alone, without the 'no': before: ['take cover']; line: 'no, come here' -> 'Come here.' (FOLLOW_ME). before: ['go left']; line: 'no no, stay here' -> 'Stay here.' (HOLD_POSITION). A 'no' followed by a place alone is still a correction (rule 3): before: ['shoot that window']; line: 'no, over there' -> 'Shoot over there.' (OPEN_FIRE). A bare 'no' stays 'no'.

4c. 'Another', 'another one', 'the other one', 'that one too', 'the next one' after an order on a thing is the same order on another thing of that kind, the word kept: before: ['shoot that window']; line: 'another' -> 'Shoot another window.' (OPEN_FIRE). before: ['hold the north door']; line: 'now the other one' -> 'Hold the other door.' (HOLD_ANGLE). before: ['grab a rifle']; line: 'another one' -> 'Grab another rifle.' (MOVE_TO). 'One more', 'once more', 'more' stay repeats (rule 1b), written back as they are.
